# General Instructions

- Reading time – 5 minutes
- Working time – 3 hours
- Write using black pen
- Draw diagrams using pencil
- Calculators approved by NESA may be used

**Total marks: 100**

# Section I – Multiple Choice (20 marks)

*Allow about 35 minutes for this section*

## Question 1
Which scientist's investigations were used for the development of the microwave oven?

A. Fleischmann  
B. Smolyanitsky  
C. Spencer  
D. van Helmont

## Question 2
Some parents claim that playing classical music will enhance their child's intelligence.

What is the name given to this claim?

A. The halo effect  
B. The Mozart effect  
C. The Doppler effect  
D. The Hawthorne effect

## Question 3
What observation led to Edward Jenner's development of a vaccine for smallpox?

A. The smallpox virus had an incubation period of 1–2 weeks.  
B. People with smallpox developed a rash and blisters containing pus.  
C. People given the smallpox vaccine did not develop the symptoms of smallpox.  
D. Milkmaids exposed to cowpox did not generally show symptoms of smallpox.

## Question 4
The graph shows the total distance travelled by airline passengers globally, and the number of airline accidents resulting in fatalities.

![Graph showing airline passenger distance traveled and fatal accidents from 1936-2016. The graph has two y-axes - left showing total distance (× 10^12 km) from 0-7, right showing fatal airline accidents per year from 0-70. The solid line shows total distance traveled increasing from near 0 in 1936 to about 7 in 2016. The dashed line shows fatal accidents fluctuating between 20-60 from 1936-2000, then declining to about 20 by 2016.](2020-images/question-4-airline-statistics-graph.png)

Which row in the table summarises the general trends in the data shown in the graph?

| | Total distance travelled | Number of fatal accidents |
|---|---|---|
| A. | Increases | Decreases |
| B. | Increases | Increases |
| C. | Decreases | Increases |
| D. | Decreases | Decreases |

## Question 5
Aboriginal Peoples have known of the medicinal properties of tea-tree oil for thousands of years, but this has not been acknowledged as their cultural and intellectual property.

A company wants to develop a new drug formulation using tea-tree oil. Which of the following is the most ethical response to the information given?

A. Scientists conduct a review to ensure that tea-tree oil has not been used in a similar formulation.  
B. Scientists analyse the active ingredients in tea-tree oil and apply to an ethics committee to allow testing of the new formulation.  
C. Aboriginal Peoples are consulted and offered a governance role in the company, with an economic agreement for the use of the knowledge.  
D. Aboriginal Peoples are consulted to help determine the best formulation to use, then the company's scientists apply for patents to protect the formulation.

## Question 6
A researcher conducted a double-blind trial to determine the effectiveness of a new cancer drug. Patients involved in the trial were assigned randomly to receive either a placebo or the new drug.

Which row of the table shows who should be aware of the drug allocation in the double-blind trial?

| | Patients | Researcher |
|---|---|---|
| A. | Yes | Yes |
| B. | Yes | No |
| C. | No | Yes |
| D. | No | No |

## Question 7
*Clostridium difficile* is a pathogenic bacteria often found in the human gut. It causes a common, life threatening illness. One treatment is for a doctor to conduct a faecal transplant, where the gut microbes from the patient are removed and a faecal sample from a healthy human is inserted, re-populating the patient's gut with beneficial microbes.

What measure must be taken to ensure the success of this type of transplant?

A. The faeces to be transplanted must be sterilised.  
B. The faeces to be transplanted must not contain pathogens.  
C. The donor must be chosen from immediate family members of the patient.  
D. The patient must be on a cranberry gut cleansing diet prior to the transplant.

## Question 8
A new drug was tested on six healthy humans. They all immediately became very sick.

What step should have been taken to ensure this was an ethical investigation?

A. Choose the subjects randomly  
B. Pay subjects for their participation  
C. Inform subjects of possible side effects  
D. Choose subjects with highly effective immune systems

## Question 9
An experiment was conducted where several small plots with the same soil type were prepared. Some were planted with a single crop species (monospecies) and some were planted with a variety of crop species (multispecies).

They were all exposed to the same weather conditions. Soil biomass was measured before and after the growing period of the crops.

Which row in the table identifies variables in this experiment?

| | The independent variable | A controlled variable |
|---|---|---|
| A. | Biomass | Monospecies or multispecies crop |
| B. | Biomass | Soil type |
| C. | Monospecies or multispecies crop | Weather conditions |
| D. | Monospecies or multispecies crop | Biomass |

## Question 10
A student compared the claims made on the labels of two health supplements.

![Two supplement bottles side by side. Product P shows: "Remarkable results in 28 days, Supplements gut health, Contains B vitamins". Product Q shows: "High strength ingredients, Supports digestive health, Relieves indigestion and heartburn, Contains 60 capsules"](2020-images/question-10-supplement-bottles.png)

Which of the following is a correct statement about the claims made on the labels?

A. Both products make a claim that can be proven.  
B. All claims made by Product P are evidence-based.  
C. Both products are equally effective at improving gut health.  
D. All claims made by Product Q can be tested by using a randomised double-blind study.

## Question 11
A laboratory experiment was conducted in a closed system where iron was added to ocean water and the population of phytoplankton (microscopic aquatic plants) and carbon dioxide levels were measured daily. The results are shown.

The iron was added on Day 3 of the experiment.

![Graph showing phytoplankton population over 10 days, with population (mg m^-3) on y-axis (0-14) and time in days on x-axis (0-10). Line shows population staying at 1 from days 0-3, then rapidly increasing to 12 by day 9](2020-images/question-11-phytoplankton-graph.png)

| Time (days) | Carbon dioxide level (ppm) |
|---|---|
| 0 | 415 |
| 1 | 415 |
| 2 | 415 |
| 3 | 415 |
| 4 | 401 |
| 5 | 387 |
| 6 | 360 |
| 7 | 310 |
| 8 | 290 |
| 9 | 280 |

What conclusion can be drawn from the results shown in the graph and table?

A. An increase in the amount of iron led to an increase in carbon dioxide levels.  
B. The iron led to an increase in the phytoplankton population and a decrease in the carbon dioxide levels.  
C. The iron caused a decrease in carbon dioxide levels which led to an increase in phytoplankton photosynthesis and population growth.  
D. The phytoplankton population would continue to increase and the carbon dioxide levels would continue to decrease over the next two days.

## Question 12
A student found the following information that could be used to predict the intensity of industrial fires.

Intensity of fire (kW/m) = Heat yield (J/g) × Fuel load (kg/m²) × Rate of spread (m/s)

| Estimated fire intensity (kW/m) | Impact on building |
|---|---|
| < 500 | Smoke detected |
| 1000 | Pallets charred |
| 5000 | Flames detected |
| > 7000 | Roof of factory on fire |

The student researched a fire in a large warehouse that contained new hardwood timber pallets with an approximate heat yield of 17 000 J/g and an estimated fuel load of 11 kg/m². Flames had been reported inside the factory but the roof was not on fire.

Using the above data, approximately how far would the fire travel each second?

A. 0.0053 m  
B. 0.027 m  
C. 37 m  
D. 190 m

## Questions 13-15
*Use the information provided to answer Questions 13-15.*

An analogue thermometer and a digital temperature probe were both placed in water that was at exactly 0°C and then in water that was at exactly 100°C. The readings for each device were recorded and the procedure was repeated.

| Device | Reading in 0°C water (°C) | | Reading in 100°C water (°C) | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | Trial 1 | Trial 2 | Trial 1 | Trial 2 |
| Analogue thermometer | −0.5 | −0.5 | 99.5 | 99.5 |
| Digital temperature probe | 5.37 | 5.37 | 105.59 | 105.59 |

## Question 13
What is the best explanation for the differences in readings on the devices compared to the exact temperature of the water?

A. Human errors  
B. Parallax errors  
C. Random errors  
D. Systematic errors

## Question 14
Based on the information provided, which statement about the devices is correct?

A. The analogue thermometer is as reliable as the digital temperature probe.  
B. The analogue thermometer is as accurate as the digital temperature probe.  
C. The analogue thermometer is less reliable than the digital temperature probe.  
D. The analogue thermometer is more accurate than the digital temperature probe.

## Question 15
These devices were then used to measure the temperature of a gas sample. The reading on the digital temperature probe was 55.48°C.

Which row of the table shows the values closest to the actual temperature of the gas sample and the temperature reading on the analogue thermometer?

| | Actual temperature of gas sample (°C) | Reading on the analogue thermometer (°C) |
|---|---|---|
| A. | 50 | 50.5 |
| B. | 50 | 49.5 |
| C. | 61 | 61.5 |
| D. | 61 | 60.5 |

## Questions 17-18
*Use the information provided to answer Questions 17 and 18.*

Students conducted an experiment to investigate the relationship between the speed of an object and the distance that it travels.

1. They rolled a marble down a ramp.
2. The marble then rolled across a bench and off the end of the bench.
3. A data logger measured the speed of the marble as it reached the end of the bench.
4. The students measured the horizontal distance from the end of the bench to where the marble landed on the floor.

![Diagram showing experimental setup with a ramp leading to a bench, with a data logger at the end of the bench. The marble's path is shown going down the ramp, across the bench, and falling to the floor. The horizontal distance traveled from the bench is labeled.](2020-images/question-17-18-marble-experiment.png)

What must be kept the same in each trial of the experiment?

A. The height of the bench  
B. The mass of the marble used  
C. The release point on the ramp  
D. The angle of inclination of the ramp

## Question 19
The table shows the number of deaths from three diseases before and after the implementation of vaccination programs. The comparisons are made over similar periods of time.

| Disease | Deaths before vaccination program | Deaths after vaccination program |
|---|---|---|
| Measles | 542 000 | 122 000 |
| Polio | 350 000 | 1 315 |
| Tetanus | 200 000 | 48 000 |

Based on the information provided, which row of the table correctly compares the percentage effectiveness of the vaccination programs?

| | Most effective | Least effective |
|---|---|---|
| A. | Measles | Tetanus |
| B. | Polio | Measles |
| C. | Tetanus | Polio |
| D. | Polio | Tetanus |

## Question 20
A recent study examined the combined effect of high-dose vitamin C and conventional cancer treatment on human brain tumour cells.

Results from this study are shown.

![Three bar graphs showing fraction of cells that survive treatment for Brain tumour cells Type 1, Type 2, and Normal brain cells. Each graph shows four bars: Control (dotted), Vitamin C (solid black), Conventional treatment (diagonal lines), and Combined treatments (light dotted). Combined treatments show the lowest survival fraction for tumor cells but similar survival for normal cells.](2020-images/question-20-vitamin-c-treatment-graphs.png)

Using the information above, which row of the table is correct?

| | Conclusion | Reason for drawing the conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| A. | The effect of vitamin C varies between Type 1 and Type 2 brain tumour cells | Conventional treatment has the same effect on Type 1 and Type 2 brain tumour cells |
| B. | Vitamin C decreased the tumours in patients | There was a decrease in the fraction of tumour cells surviving after combined treatments were applied |
| C. | Combined treatments are the most effective in treating brain tumour patients | Combined treatments decreased the number of brain tumour cells more than the other treatments |
| D. | Vitamin C is effective without conventional tumour treatment | Brain tumour cells decreased in number by the application of vitamin C more significantly than when treated with conventional treatments alone |

## Question 32 (12 marks)
A student is researching climate change and wrote summaries of three pieces of information.

**Student summary 1: An article from a daily newspaper in 2019**

An astrophysicist stated that when water vapour levels rise, so does global air temperature, as shown in the graph. This relationship has been verified by other scientists.

![Graph showing variation from average for water vapour (solid line) and global air temperature (dashed line) from 1988-2014. Both lines show similar fluctuating patterns, generally moving together.](2020-images/question-32-climate-graph.png)

The astrophysicist suggested that water vapour is the main contributor to climate change, while carbon dioxide is only a minor contributor to the greenhouse effect.

Another scientist said this is misleading since increasing air temperatures cause increased evaporation. Therefore increasing carbon dioxide levels can still lead to increased water vapour.

Later the article mentions that the astrophysicist's work is paid for by oil companies.

**Student summary 2: Review of the same article by scientists**

Scientists reviewing the newspaper article stated that it used flawed reasoning and gave a single scientist's conclusion the same value as the findings of the majority of scientists.

The organisation that published this review stated that it is an 'unbiased, non-profit organisation'.

**Student summary 3: Quotation**

'It's not climate change that needs to be tackled. It is the political power of the fossil fuel industry.'

RICHARD DENNISS  
Chief Economist  
The Australia Institute

© Dr Richard Denniss, Chief Economist. Reproduced by permission of the Australia Institute
